name: Scotland
summary: A white saltire, the cross of Saint Andrew, on a blue field. Legend dates it to a battle in the 9th century, which would make it one of the oldest national flags in use.
origin: According to legend, in 832 King Óengus II of the Picts saw a white saltire against the blue sky before a battle against the Angles at Athelstaneford, and adopted the cross after his victory.

The saltire was used as a Scottish emblem from at least the 14th century, and a white saltire on blue is recorded on Scottish flags from the 16th century. In 1606 it was combined with St George's Cross to form the first Union Flag.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sky of the legend; the Scottish Parliament recommends Pantone 300.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The cross of clouds in the legend.

symbols.name: Saltire
symbols.meaning: St Andrew, patron saint of Scotland, who by tradition was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

facts: St Andrew's Day, 30 November, is Scotland's national day.
The Royal Banner (the Lion Rampant) is the monarch's banner in Scotland, not the national flag.
Nova Scotia's flag is the saltire with colours reversed.
clues: A white diagonal cross on blue.
A legend says it appeared in the sky before a 9th-century battle.
Its saint was crucified on an X-shaped cross.
